back_translation: Woe to the bloody city, full of lies and plunder, never without prey!
Hear the crack of the whip, the rumble of wheels, galloping horses, and bounding chariots!
Charging horsemen, flashing swords and glittering spears, a multitude of slain, heaps of corpses, bodies without end—people stumble over the corpses.
All this is because of the many harlotries of the alluring, graceful prostitute, mistress of sorceries, who betrays nations with her harlotries and peoples with her sorceries.
The LORD of Hosts declares: Behold, I am against you. I will lift your skirts over your face; I will show the nations your nakedness and the kingdoms your shame.
I will throw filth on you and treat you with contempt; I will make you a spectacle.
Then all who see you will flee from you and say, 'Nineveh is laid waste! Who will mourn for her?' Where shall I find comforters for you?
Are you better than Thebes, which sat by the Nile with water around her, whose rampart was the sea and whose wall was the waters?
Cush and Egypt were her boundless strength; Put and Libya were her allies.
Yet she was carried away into exile; her little children were dashed to pieces at the head of every street; they cast lots for her nobles, and all her great men were bound in chains.
You too will become drunk; you will hide yourself; you will seek refuge from the enemy.
All your fortresses are like fig trees with first-ripe figs—when shaken, they fall into the mouth of the eater.
Behold, your troops are like women in your midst; the gates of your land are thrown wide open to your enemies; fire devours your bars.
Draw water for the siege; strengthen your fortresses; go down into the clay and tread the mortar; repair the brick kiln.
There the fire will devour you, the sword will cut you off; it will consume you like the young locust. Multiply yourselves like the young locust, multiply like the swarming locust!
You have increased your merchants beyond the stars of heaven, but the young locust strips its skin and flies away.
Your guards are like locusts, and your nobles like clouds of locusts that settle on the walls on a cold day; but when the sun rises, they fly away, and no one knows where they are.
O king of Assyria, your shepherds slumber and your nobles lie down; your people are scattered on the mountains, with no one to gather them.
There is no relief for your wound; your injury is grievous. All who hear the news of you clap their hands over you, for who has not felt your endless cruelty?
